Brief facts of the present case are that on 05.07.2015, at about 11.15 A.M, the petitioner was travelling on a motor cycle bearing No. DL8SND2225 as a pillion ( The vs Harun Khan on 15 May, 2023 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/21891894/
5 rider, being driven by his son Vikas Yadav.

When they were proceedings from Sheetla Mata Mandir Gurgaon towards Dwarka via Palam Vihar and reached just ahead of Bhagat Singh Chowk, Sector5, Gurgaon, Haryana suddenly a dumper ( Truck)
bearing No. HR55P9031 came from behind and hit the motor cycle forcefully.
As a result of forceful impact both the occupant of motorcycle fell down on the road and petitioner sustained severe head injuries besides other injuries.
He was immediately removed to Fortis Hospital, Gurgaon for his treatment.
The petitioner has also been treated at BLK Hospital Pusa Road N Delhi.

2. The respondent No.1 and 2 have filed their WS stating therein that no accident has been caused by the respondent No.1 as alleged in the petition and the alleged FIR has falsely been lodged by the police against respondent No.1 in collusion with the petitioner.

3. The respondent No3 has also filed its WS stating therein that accident had occurred due to negligent driving of motorcycle bearing No. DL8SND 2225 and not due any negligence of alleged offending vehicle No. HR55P 9031.
It is stated that at the most the present case is of contributory negligence on the part of injured and his driver.

ISSUE No.1: Whether petitioner Hans Raj Yadav sustained injuries in a motor vehicle accident dt.

8.
The onus to prove this issue was upon the petitioner.

To prove the present issue , the petitioner has examined PW2 Sh Vikas Yadav, who in his affidavit (Ex. PW2/A) has deposed that on 05.07.2015, at about 11.15 A.M, he was proceeding towards his house from Sheetla Mata Mandir Gurgaon alongwith his father on a motor cycle bearing No. DL8SND 2225.
He was driving the motorcycle while his father was travelling as a pillion rider.
He has deposed that when they reached just ahead of Bhagat Singh Chowk, Sector5, Gurgaon, Haryana.
Suddenly a dumper ( Truck) MACT No.127/16 Hansraj Yadav vs Harun Khan & ors Page No. 7 of 17 bearing No. HR55P9031 came from behind and hit the motor cycle forcefully.

sentences.text: As a result of forceful impact they fell down on the road and his father sustained severe head injuries besides other injuries.
He has removed his father to Fortis Hospital, Gurgaon for his treatment.
PW2 deposed that accident caused due to sole negligence on the part of driver, who was driving vehicle No. HR55P9031 in rash and negligent manner.
9. PW 2 has been duly crossexamined.
But the testimony of PW2 with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of offending vehicles could not be impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
Moreover after investigation, police indicted respondent no.1 as accused for the offences punishable under Sections 279/338 of IPC.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1.
The respondent No.1 has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his alleged false implication, if any.
The fact respondent no. 1 is facing the trial as an accused in a criminal case is not disputed.
Even otherwise strict rule that negligence is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is not to be proved in MACT proceedings.

Considering all these facts, it is proved on record that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a truck bearing registration no. HR 55 P 9031 by respondent no.1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.

10. The issue is decided in favour of the petitioner and against respondents by holding that petitioner suffered injuries in a vehicular accident by truck bearing registration no. HR 55 P 9031 driven by respondent no.1 in rash and negligent manner.

The submission of Ld Counsel for the Insurance company is that the injured was not wearing helmet at the time of accident so it amount to a contributory negligence on his part and as such the Insurance Company is not liable to pay the compensation to the petitioner.

The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs Surinder Singh & Ors in Appeal ( Civil) 3321 of 2008 has held that "
The question of contributory negligence would arise only when both the parties are found to be negligent".

entities.text: Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs Surinder Singh & Ors in Appeal ( Civil) 3321 of 2008
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: But here in the present case the offending truck hit the motor cycle of injured from behind.

This Tribunal is of the view, that mere not wearing helmet may only violation of Motor Vehicle Act but it does not give any right to the driver of offending vehicle to hit the motorcycle of injured and caused him injuries.

13. Another argument tendered by Ld Counsel for the Insurance Company is that the petitioner has not taken Voluntary retirement due to injuries being sustained in Motor Vehicle accident, as alleged but he opted Voluntary retirement scheme.

To counter this arguments, Ld Counsel for the petitioner has argued that the injuries being sustained by the petitioner in the accident has made him disabled to render service of Para Military Force and for this reason he has taken Voluntary retirement.
14. After considering the submissions being raised by Ld Counsel for the Insurance company as well as Ld Counsel for the petitioner.
The perusal of record, particularly the testimony of PW4 Dr Deepak Kumar, the petitioner is not in a position to work as official of Para Military Force due to infirmity developed in his body.

In that circumstances, the Voluntary MACT No.127/16 Hansraj Yadav vs Harun Khan & ors Page No. 9 of 17 retirement taken by the petitioner is justifiable and same may be termed a retirement taken due to inability to perform in Para Military Force.

Hence ,
seeing nature of injuries and disability suffered by petitioner as well as his admission in various hospitals, a lump sum amount of Rs. 4,00,000/ is granted to him as compensation towards medical expenses.

Ld Counsel for the petitioner submits that petitioner was working SI GD in Central Reserve Police Force.
Though petitioner has placed on record Form16 for computing the compensation and for taking the gross salary as mentioned in Form16 Ex PW3/2.
I am not considering the same for the purpose of computation as the document Ex PW3/3 has been issued in the month of March 2016 to February 2017.
This Tribunal is assessing the income of the petitioner on the basis of last drawn salary ie January 2017 Ex PW3/ 2, when he taken Voluntary retirement.
As per last drawn salary Ex PW3/2 the gross salary of petitioner was Rs.56,772/.
An amount of Rs.4000/ p.m was being deducted as Income tax.
After deducting a sum of Rs.4,000/ the monthly income of the petitioner has been assessed to Rs.52,772/ p.m for computation of compensation.
As per Ex PW3/5 the petitioner remained on leave for about 540 days till his Voluntary retirement, in August 2017.
Out of which petitioner received pay for 300 days and remained on without pay leave for 240 days.

As per PW4 Dr Deepak Kumar, that due to grievous head injuries the petitioner/injured developed behavioral disturbances in the form of irritability, unprovoked aggression, disinhibited behavior and inability to maintain activities of daily living without assistance due to head injury sustained in road traffic accident.
PW2 Vikas Yadav, son of the petitioner has deposed that his father ( petitioner) is not in his full senses and is unable to inform the attendant to ease out or his desire to attend nature calls.
He has deposed that sometimes petitioner gets so irritated and he started murmur irrelevant things to himself and has become hard of hearing and unable to speak properly.
18. As per disability certificate of the petitioner he has suffered 83% permanent disability.

And in view of paragraph no. 61 (iv) of judgment in National Insurance Company Limited vs. Pranay Sethi & Ors, SLP (Civil) No. 25590 of 2014, decided on 31.10.2017 and the judgment of Hon'ble Delhi High Court in case of Sanjay Oberoi vs Manoj Bageriya, MAC Appeal no.829/2011 decided on 03.11.2017, the injured would be MACT No.127/16 Hansraj Yadav vs Harun Khan & ors Page No. 11 of 17 entitled to an addition of 30% of the established income.

opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
But the testimony of PW2 with respect to accident and rash & negligent driving of offending vehicles could not be impeached.
Even otherwise, the proof of negligence while disposing of a claim under MACT is not that strict as it is for the offence under Section 279/337/338 of IPC.
The evidence which has come on the file can be considered and becomes more relevant when there is no specific evidence led by other side in rebuttal.
The FIR has been registered against respondent no.1.
The respondent No.1 has not filed any complaint against the police before any higher authority against his alleged false implication, if any.
The fact respondent no. 1 is facing the trial as an accused in a criminal case is not disputed.
Even otherwise strict rule that negligence is to be proved beyond reasonable doubt is not to be proved in MACT proceedings.
Considering all these facts, it is proved on record that accident in question was caused due to rash or negligent driving of a truck bearing registration no. HR 55 P 9031 by respondent no.1 thereby causing injuries to the petitioner.
The Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs Surinder Singh & Ors in Appeal ( Civil) 3321 of 2008 has held that "
The question of contributory negligence would arise only when both the parties are found to be negligent".
So a lumpsum amount of Rs. 73,02,000/ is allowed to petitioner, as loss of future earnings,
due to permanent disability.
After the accident, petitioner was taken to various hospitals.
It is very much apparent that when a person is leading a normal life and suddenly meets with an MACT No.127/16 Hansraj Yadav vs Harun Khan &
ors Page No. 12 of 17 accident which changes his complete life, the mental agony which he or she faces cannot be considered.
The physical pain which petitioner had undergone after the accident cannot be explained as to a miserable person every body sympathizes though it never pacifies a victim.
So this Tribunal while relying upon the judgment of Hon'ble High Court in Jyoti Singh Vs Nand Kishore & Ors ; MAC APP 870/2011 is of the view that one attendant is required to look after the petitioner round the clock.
So far as disfiguration is concerned, petitioner is a case of permanent disability to the extent 83%
and he must have faced mental agony due to the accident.

opennyai_summary.arguments:
Being injured, petitioner is well within his rights to claim compensation.
But here in the present case the offending truck hit the motor cycle of injured from behind.
This Tribunal is of the view, that mere not wearing helmet may only violation of Motor Vehicle Act but it does not give any right to the driver of offending vehicle to hit the motorcycle of injured and caused him injuries.
In that circumstances, the Voluntary MACT No.127/16 Hansraj Yadav vs Harun Khan & ors Page No. 9 of 17 retirement taken by the petitioner is justifiable and same may be termed a retirement taken due to inability to perform in Para Military Force.
